I, the one writing these lines, am a dead man. I am dead quite officially, in full accordance with the law: I died and was not buried. Ask those who saw the final minutes of the recording about me, and they will tell you that I became one of the victims of that house; that after the night of the investigation I was never found, neither alive nor dead; that in the reports my name has long been listed among the missing. And yet — I am here. I breathe. I hear my own voice. I remember the cold of the door handle, the smell of damp in the corridor, and the moment I understood: the house did not want to kill me. It wanted to leave me inside — in endless madness.

God Is Not Here is a story-driven first-person horror game focused on a dark atmosphere, the exploration of an abandoned house, and paranormal events. The player will step inside, examine the surroundings, search for traces of what is happening, and interact with objects while gradually sinking into the story of the house.

The free demo includes the first chapter of the game and lets you enter the house where it all began.

God of Stock is a stock-market deck-building roguelike. Start with $100 and use god-blessed cards to trade stocks, manipulate prices, and turn market chaos into profit. Build a powerful deck, collect artifacts and treasures, and grow your fortune to $1,000,000 to become the God of Stock.

Manipulate the Market

Play trading and spell cards to control prices, engineer market swings, and profit from the chaos you create.

Build a Market-Breaking Deck

Combine cards, stock abilities, artifacts, news effects, and treasures to create powerful trading strategies.

Survive Rising Debt

You have five trading days to reach your target. Every week brings a larger goal—and more debt waiting to collect.

Choose Your God

Each god transforms how you trade, from aggressive short-selling and rapid speculation to dividends and long-term investing.

Features:

  • 5 playable gods with 5 different trading styles.

  • 400+ cards across five gods and neutral card pools.

  • 80+ powerful artifacts to uncover.

  • 50+ stocks to trade, each with unique abilities.

  • 50+ news events that can reshape the market.

  • 60+ weekend locations to help build your deck.

Match runes. Channel the gods. One life per run.

A match-3 roguelite RPG set in Greek myth: nine realms, one life, and a board that fights back.

Match runes, command the battle

Skulls strike, hearts heal, shields soak, coloured runes bank mana. Match four to blast a row and column, five to wipe a colour.

Every foe has a tell

Each enemy hides an elemental weakness and a resistance, revealed only as you fight. Read it and your damage leaps.

Build a run, choose the road

Seven demigods, a boon at every level, relics that rewrite how you fight, and a Merchant before every boss.

Die. Keep the legend.

Death relocks the realms but never takes your feats or your Favor.

Features

  • Weaknesses and resistances you find only by fighting

  • Seven demigods, 25 boons and 60 relics

  • Nine realms, 60 battles, telegraphed boss specials

  • 20 to 40 minute runs, plus a Daily gauntlet

  • One purchase, no microtransactions, no timers

  • Fifteen Ascension rungs, 66 feats, a leaderboard, full controller support

Match. Cast. Conquer. The gods are watching.

The classic Gold Miner, now with company.

Gold Miner: Party Rush throws 2 to 6 players into the same frantic gold rush — the same physics-based crane you remember, the same satisfying thunk of a massive nugget, and now someone else going for the same thing at the same time.

Compete across multiple rounds, grab everything you can, and come out on top. Easy to pick up. Impossible to stay calm.

Key Features

  • 2–6 player online multiplayer — share the chaos with friends or get matched with players around the world in seconds

  • Classic Gold Miner gameplay rebuilt for head-to-head competition

  • Multi-round matches — scores accumulate, tension builds, and comebacks happen

  • Quick Play for instant casual sessions whenever you feel like a dig

  • Ranked Mode & Competitive Ladder — five tiers from Bronze to Grandmaster, for miners who take their rivalry seriously

Golden Trivia Show is a quiz game presented as a TV show that you can play solo or cooperatively with your friends online (up to 4 players). You start with a pile of gold bars and need to avoid losing them. Each question has 4 possible answers, and you can choose to divide your gold bars among them. Only the gold bars placed on the correct answer will remain with you; the rest will fall into a pool filled with piranhas. If you manage to make it to the end and win some gold, you can spend it on cool new suits and cosmetics.

· Enter a TV-style quiz show

· 1–4 players (online co-op)

· 1,000+ questions with both text and images

· Not sure which is the correct answer? Divide your gold bars among them

· Win gold and customize your character

Build a golf course on raw land. Watch a full field of golfers play it. See where they struggle, change the hole, and watch again. Then run the club that grows around it.

You're the architect. You arrive on a raw piece of land: hills, water, trees, open ground and tight corners, and it's on you to see what it could become. Where does the first tee sit? Does the green tuck into that hollow, or does the fairway bend around the water instead? You're standing on unbuilt land like the great golf architects of old, and now it's your turn.

Build it

  • Sculpt the terrain. Raise hills, dig valleys, carve ponds, streams and waterfalls until the land supports the course you're picturing.

  • Lay out each hole by hand. Set the tee, choose the line to the green, and decide whether it's a tricky par 3 or a long par 5 that makes golfers think.

  • Paint freehand, no grid. Fairway, rough, green, bunker, water and more, straight onto the ground. Save a layout and stamp it for quick designs.

  • Plan the whole property. Practice green, driving range, clubhouse amenities, and the trees and land around it all.

Watch them play it

  • A full field on a real shot model. Clubs, wind, slopes and skill all matter. Golfers read your hole and choose their line: some take on the bunker, some lay up short of it.

  • A course that comes alive. Golfers mark their balls, crouch to read putts and fix their pitch marks. At dawn your crew sets the pins, mows fresh stripes and empties the bins.

  • Big moments. Drain a long putt for a banner and confetti. Every ace gets fireworks, a replay and a spot on the Aces wall.

  • Watch the Broadcast. Sit back and follow the field live, with a commentary team in the booth.

See what works, then fix it

  • The heatmap shows where golfers land and where they get into trouble, so you can see whether that bunker actually changed how the hole plays.

  • Every hole is scored on how it looks and how it plays, and a hazard where golfers actually land counts for more than one nobody reaches. A pretty hole that plays badly is a problem you can see and fix.

Run the club

  • Green fees, members, staff, a pro shop and a touring beverage cart.

  • Hire a Head Pro who gives lessons on the range and sells more in the pro shop.

  • Host tournaments, and enter the Club Championship yourself.

  • Grow across a region: buy more land, build a course on each plot, and run them all from one wallet.

  • Sandbox mode with unlimited money, if you'd rather just build.

Play it yourself

  • Play As: take the shots yourself on your own layout, with a swing meter, a putt read and a rangefinder.

  • Wildlife wanders the property, and photo mode captures the course at its best.

Also

  • Full controller support.

  • Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel).

  • English, plus six more languages translated by machine. We'll fund a proper human translation for any language that turns out to be popular in Early Access.

  • Metric or imperial units.

This is no longer first-move-wins, one-move-each traditional Gomoku (five in a row).

Gomoklear is a connect-five-to-clear Gomoku strategy roguelike. Form a five, and the whole line leaves the board; new pieces land and spawn; pieces are moved, removed, transformed—the board rewrites on the spot. Two plays a Round, one for the Rival. Collect powered pieces and Manuscripts, build your Library at Serendipity and the Stall.

In Gomoklear, every piece carries a different power:

spawn new pieces around it when placed, shove aside Enemy pieces that hem you in, or remove them from the board outright. Turn Enemy pieces to your side, gain extra Turns to play, even reshape the Field…

In the chaos these powered pieces make, Gomoku Lines fire again and again. Within the Round Limit, chase a higher count!

Choose a Playstyle at the start, and take a distinct starting Library and Manuscript with you.

After a Match, collect new pieces and grow your Library;

at the Stall, buy Manuscripts and pick the pieces you want.

Stargazing, wagers, arena bouts… make your choice in Serendipity, and walk away with rewards unlike any other.

  • A new Gomoku rhythm: two plays for you, one for the Rival. Complete multiple Gomoku Lines within the Round Limit.

  • Playstyles, each its own school.

  • Eight Color Schemes, a hundred-odd powered pieces.

  • Manuscripts grant run-wide bonuses; Serendipity and the Stall enrich the run.

  • Matches, Famous Matches, Final Matches—Rival Abilities all differ.

Step into Gomoklear, and explore a new kind of Gomoku.

Shove your friends off the bed to get a good night's sleep. Good Night is a PvP party game where you fight by tossing and turning.

Controls

Roll, squirm, and shove. Of course, you cannot move the way you want because you are sleeping. If your sleeping posture becomes messy, calm down. Reset.

Modes & Stages

There are two modes. Survival: fight to be the last one still in bed. Endless: kick down other players within the time limit and get points. The stages: it's not just a simple double bed. There are also a giant bed, an ice bed, and a bed which falls down. The players are crazy. They don't care where they sleep.

Best Shots

The funniest moment is recorded automatically. When the match is over, check the weird posture. Maybe someone becomes a mess.

King Sleeper

You win the battles with bad manners. Congratulations, you can become the King Sleeper. Misbehave yourself.

Multiplayer

Play Online with remote friends, or locally with friends in the same room for up to four people.

Aim for comfortable sleep with wobbly posture and take the throne of King Sleeper.

The city mutated overnight. The internet is down. The only business still open is a pizzeria, and you are its best customer. Years of Tommy's pizza left you so greasy the mutagen slid right off.

Now you work for him.

Gore Grind is a first-person roguelite horde shooter for 1 to 4 players in online & couch co-op. Survive the night, bank what the city drops, and spend it on guns, gadgets and the occasional second chance at life.

Up to 4 players on one couch & online. Share the street, share the loot, argue about who is worth reviving.

The horde does not come in waves. It comes like weather. Freeze it, burn it, blow it up, mop up the rest. The soundtrack is metal, obviously.

Tommy makes the pizza and hands out the work. He does not say where his money comes from, and you should not ask.

Out here, money is life. Death is not the end, it is a bill, and the bill doubles every time you die that night. Put your cash in the bank before the gnomes find it. Then maybe lose some at roulette. It is your money.

When you come back, the AI on the radio takes the credit. "Restored. You're welcome."

Turrets, barrels and other hardware of uncertain origin. The Mechanic sells it, you place it, it does the work while you reload. Where it came from is between Tommy and a guy he does not do business with.

A rogue AI tried to take over the world and lost track of it. Now it talks through every radio in town, takes credit for everything, and insists it is in charge. It is in charge of nothing.

Except the Crankers. It imagines its own riders of the apocalypse so hard they show up and hit you, and it announces each one by chapter and verse.

Then there are the gnomes. Nobody knows what they are. They take your money and vanish.

  • Buy a Hog at the Mechanic's garage and race him across town.

  • Deliver pizza between shifts. It is still a business.

  • Every night ends when its boss dies. Not one second before.

And all this for a slice of gabagool.

A STORY THAT CONTINUES...

Gorgeous Baby Bella is the first chapter of a larger psychological horror story.

Not every mystery has an answer yet. Bella's true nature, the events surrounding Liora, and the secrets hidden within the apartment will gradually unfold in the continuation of the story.

🧹 Daily Chores

  • Take care of Liora's daily chores and keep her home clean and tidy. Pick up the trash, clean up the mess, and take care of the household tasks.

🌙 In the Dark

  • The silence of the house is not always comforting. You never know what you might encounter in the dark.

🏠 People

  • Meet the people around you and engage in pleasant conversations with them. Alongside quality and meaningful dialogue, you will sometimes experience moments that stir different emotions.

Grand Snow Rider is an open-world action-adventure simulator about fighting your way through an extreme snowstorm.

Take on the role of Lucy and set out to recover abandoned vehicles scattered across snow-covered locations. Clear blocked roads, locate missing cars and their keys, fight off troublemakers, and bring every recovered vehicle back to safety.

But there’s a catch: the more progress you make, the worse the weather gets.

CLEAR YOUR OWN PATH

Snow isn't just scenery — it's part of the gameplay.

Deep snow can slow Lucy down, block roads, and leave vehicles completely stuck. Take control of snow-clearing machinery and carve your own routes through buried roads and paths to reach abandoned vehicles.

FIND THE CAR. FIND THE KEY. BRING IT BACK.

Finding a vehicle is only the beginning.

Mark its location on your GPS, track down the hidden key, and be ready to fight for it. Local troublemakers aren't going to stand by and let you take their prize without a snowball fight.

Win, and you can return to the vehicle and drive it back to the parking area.

Lose? Well... you'll have to go get that key again.

SNOWBALLS ARE WEAPONS

Nobody needs real bullets here.

Fight groups of troublemakers in snowball battles and use your equipment to gain the upper hand. They can knock Lucy down, steal the key, and send you right back to where you started.

Get back up, return to the fight, and finish the job.

FOUR GADGETS. FOUR DIFFERENT TOOLS.

Lucy has access to four unusual gadgets, each designed for a different problem.

Fight enemies, melt snow, free frozen vehicles, and manipulate cars when brute force isn't enough. Choosing the right tool can make recovering the next vehicle considerably easier.

EVERY CAR HAS A STORY

The vehicles you recover aren't just numbers on a checklist.

Throughout each mission, Jay stays in contact with Lucy over the radio, sharing stories about the cars you discover and the people who owned them.

What begins as another recovery job gradually becomes a journey through the lives of people caught in the storm.

FROM A PARK TO AN ENTIRE STATE

Your journey takes place across three increasingly large locations:

Park → City → State

Start small in the park, move on to the city, and eventually face the storm across a much larger region.

As the search area grows, you'll need to change your approach — and find new ways to locate vehicles buried somewhere in the snow-covered world.

THE STORM KEEPS GETTING WORSE

Every vehicle you recover and register brings you one step closer to completing the job.

At the same time, the snowfall intensifies.

Visibility gets worse. Snow gets deeper. Roads become harder to navigate, and both Lucy and her vehicles become increasingly vulnerable to getting stuck.

Find the cars. Recover the keys. Clear the roads. Bring them home — before the storm takes over.

Build Your Dream Hotel

Start with a small family hotel and transform it into a towering luxury destination.

Build new floors, upgrade rooms and services, manage staff, and keep guests moving smoothly through reception and elevators. Every decision affects your hotel’s growth, income and reputation.

Grow From One Star to Five

Meet inspection requirements, earn new hotel stars and unlock increasingly prestigious facilities. After reaching five stars, continue developing your hotel toward the ultimate Palace status.

Build and Upgrade Your Hotel

Expand upward with room floors and improve reception, elevators and facilities. Balance capacity, efficiency and cost as your hotel grows from a modest beginning into a vast hospitality empire.

Create Facilities Guests Want to Visit

Build restaurants, gyms, conference floors, spas, an Event Hall and a casino. Each facility has its own role, capacity and upgrade path, giving you new ways to attract guests, increase satisfaction and earn income.

Host Conferences and Major Events

Accept conference bookings, reserve rooms for multi-day groups and guide participants through your hotel. Later, host larger events such as weddings and gala-style celebrations in the Event Hall.

Keep the Hotel Running

Hire cleaners, develop your Service Floor and respond to operational problems before they disrupt the guest experience. A successful hotel needs more than beautiful rooms—it also needs reliable logistics and well-planned services.

Master Hotel Logistics

Manage guest queues, elevator traffic, room availability, staffing, facility coverage and satisfaction. Rapid expansion can be profitable, but only if the hotel can handle the pressure.

Build It Your Way

Focus on efficient growth, premium guest experiences or a huge landmark hotel. Every Grand Vista Hotel develops differently depending on the choices you make.

Begin Again With a Growing Head Start

Each time you reach Palace status, future playthroughs gain a permanent 10% bonus to income. The bonus stacks with every completed Palace run—for example, four Palace completions grant a 40% income bonus.

Language Support

Grand Vista Hotel will support 16 languages at full release, including Arabic and Ukrainian.

Please note that Arabic and Ukrainian are not currently available in the demo.

"We make our friends; we make our enemies; but God makes our next-door neighbour."

- G.K. Chesterton

Grandma Left Me a Building is a cozy apartment management sim where you restore the ruined building your grandma left you. Pick your tenants, manage neighbor dynamics, upgrade the building, hire staff, and handle the chaos that follows.


The walls are crumbling, the pipes are leaking, strange noises keep coming from upstairs. You're in for a long haul, fixing it all with the rent you collect. But the applicants knocking on your door are just as strange: do you go with the opera singer who bursts into an aria in the elevator, the philosopher who answers every question with "but why?", or the eight-year-old who takes apart anything within reach and puts it back together about 20% of the time?

As you welcome all these eccentric characters into your building, remember one thing: they have to get along. Wrong pairings bring chaos. The right ones bring peace. Fix up the place, hire staff, handle whatever the day brings. Grandma will be watching.



  • Review the lease contracts your broker brings and set the terms.
  • Place tenants in apartments with their future neighbors in mind.
  • Handle tenant requests and complaints before they pile up.
  • Fix what's broken, open new apartments, and raise the building's value.
  • Collect daily rent, pay salaries and bills on time.
  • Hire staff: doormen, security, cleaners, and more.
  • Handle unexpected events when they hit, live with the consequences.


  • 30+ unique tenants across 4 social tiers.
  • 300+ distinct character interactions.
  • 100+ unexpected events.
  • 20+ building upgrades.
  • 6 different staff types.
  • Trait-based tenant interaction system.
  • Different tenants based on your building's reputation.
  • Drag-and-drop tenant placement system.
  • Happiness-driven dynamic income system.
  • Multi-level upgrade system.
  • No time pressure, plan at your own pace.
  • Hand-drawn cartoon art.

Grave Profits is a Roguelike Auto-Battler Dungeon Crawler for Single Player and CO-OP play.  It begs for the ONE MORE RUN feeling with 20 minute runs, as you unlock new game changing relics, units, abilities and dungeons.

Build armored walls with Holy units, who sell faith for coin, and spread Fire and Poison with Eldritch Knights and Alchemists, Eat your priests with the Gargantuan Cyclops. Or create some completely unreasonable abomination between battles and hurl it at the enemy.


Each Hero approaches the journey with unique abilities, starting conditions and mechanics that transform how you build, change the rules, or even introduce completely new Alliances (like the Gnolls) to the game.

Heroes gain experience across expeditions, unlock new hero abilities and powerful Relics. These are not simple stat bonuses. RELICS alter recruitment, change card interaction, rewrite rules and some abilities can even eat opponents units, yum. 

Merge 3 cards of the same type to LEVEL UP. Strengthen your recruits further by mutating and grafting abilities, send units on side quests to gain new traits, or sacrifice units for the good of the party.

Your Steam friends victories and failures can reach into your own expeditions, even when you are not playing together.

  • Discover Abandoned Camps after a friend’s expedition was defeated in the same dungeon

  • Rescue imprisoned Units belonging to your friends

  • Face rival crawlers in battle built by your friends

  • Leave your own traces behind for other friends to discover

Random recruits, dangerous encounters, Tarot cards, Allies, Intruders and constantly changing dungeon laws force you to adapt in every run.  Build around what you find to make your way out.

But be careful, the dark is never safe, bring a torch to burn it away.

Gravefire Tavern is a roguelite backpack auto-battler that blends tavern management, spatial buildcrafting, and expedition survival. Keep the only tavern with a pale hearth alive at the edge of a cursed border, recruit adventurers, prepare their equipment, and follow the clues left by your missing brother.

The backpack is not storage. It is a battle machine.
Every Gravefire-touched item responds to position, adjacency, and connection. Arrange weapons, shields, bottles, and tools into combinations that trigger one another. Every slot you commit before departure may decide whether the party makes it home.

Run a tavern that remembers everyone
Recruit adventurers with different backgrounds and traits. Assemble a party of three, choose their formation, and prepare their loadouts. Manage the warehouse, training ground, infirmary, blacksmith, and graveyard so that every resource, wound, and lesson from one expedition strengthens the next.

Search, fight, and extract before everything is lost
Enter a borderland where roads, relics, and memories refuse to stay in place. Claim temporary loot, reorganize backpacks, and decide whether to push deeper, challenge a powerful enemy, or retreat with what you have. Only equipment that survives the return through the Gravefire truly belongs to the tavern.

Death is not the end
Adventurers can be wounded, retire, or die permanently, but their graves, histories, and traces remain. The previous party brings back brands with their lives. The next party follows those brands farther into the border.

Dark, but not hopeless.
Cute, but not childish.
Absurd, but with consequences.

The Veil tore on a Monday. The dead stopped staying dead. And Aldric — Sage of the Veil, hiding from his past in a quiet mortician's job — is the only one still on shift.

GRAVEYARD SHIFT™: A SAGE'S LAST STAND is a dark pixel-art roguelike deckbuilder where the dead on your table become the deck in your hands. Survive twenty-two nights across four weeks of escalating horrors, forge your cards toward their final Ascended forms, and find out what's been waiting behind the Veil the whole time.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚰ EVERY CORPSE IS A CHOICE

Every body on your table is a build decision.

  • BURIAL — bury up to two cards, gone forever. Travel light.

  • EMBALM — name a family. Five of its cards come out of the drawer; keep one, preserved at rank 1, and the body heals you on the way out.

  • DISSECTION — take it apart: four Veil cards and one Mystery.

  • FULL RELEASE — sever the soul and rip open a booster of possibilities: five cards, keep two, and a Friend or a Legendary may answer… but the Veil remembers every door you open.

Some corpses arrive possessed — confront what's inside and win, and a Legendary soul may fight beside you for the rest of the run. Lose, and it joins tonight's wave. And some souls give more than a card:

  • A rare GENEROUS SOUL spills ten cards across the table and lets you keep four.

  • A rarer GAMBLER'S SOUL deals ten face-down and dares you to flip three — and live with whatever you find.

And whatever the night hands you, the deck stays yours — any card you never asked for can be turned away at the gravedigger's price. It climbs with every refusal, so travel light while it's cheap.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

✦ SIX FAMILIES OF POWER

158 handcrafted cards. 67 named combos. One deck, built from the dead.

  • VENGEANCE — brutal, direct, and always swinging.

  • CHAOS — dice, gambits, and beautiful disasters.

  • WISDOM — patient engines that outlast the night.

  • PLAGUE — rot that does the killing for you.

  • VEIL — forbidden power at a forbidden price.

  • MYSTERY — true effects hidden until you dare to play them.

Chain the right cards and one of 67 named combos detonates across the screen — with a score multiplier that rewards style as much as survival.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🏆 THE FINEST SHIFTS

Three boards hang on the title, and every name on them is a door.

  • THE CLEAN MONTH — the all-time board. Your best campaign, posted as it stands.

  • THE WEEKLY — this week's contract, every player on the same terms and the same seed. A new board every Monday.

  • THE ASH PAGE — the same runs with debts signed, multiplier and all. Sealed until you've found the Ledger.

Click any name and read their shift — the deck they carried, card by card, the cards they cast most, the fight, the purse and the clock, and the Morgue upgrades, talents or terms they stood on.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📜 THE WEEKLY SHIFT

One contract a week. The same for everyone.

Every Monday a contract is posted: one debt carried all month, two boons lent by the house, one seed — the same terms for every player in the world. It's the full month, all twenty-two nights, on the house profile: no Morgue, no talents, no Ledger but these, every card in the pool. Play it as often as you like this week — your best score is the one that posts, and each run must finish before Monday's bell. An unfinished one lapses and posts nothing. Your campaign records are untouched.

☠ LET IT ROT

Not every deck kills quickly. The best ones don't have to.

Stack Poison, Bleed and Burn on a body and it dies on its own time — then Virulence swells everything already eating the creature, and Volatile Fuel pours on what's still burning. Afflictions wear a mark on the enemy so you can always read what's killing it, and the biggest horrors in the game are the ones that give a slow build the most turns to work.

⚔ THE DEAD FIGHT IN PACKS

Under the Blood Moon, targeting becomes the whole game.

A front-liner walks in shielded by a support line — healers stitching it back together, casters seeding poison into your hand's future. Cut the healer first, sweep the entire line with one blade, or burn the front-liner down before the mending outruns you. Cards that hit everything stop being a luxury and start being a plan.

🌘 THE VEIL KEEPS A LEDGER

Power is never free. It isn't even cheap.

The Veil is the deep end of the pool — the widest school in the game, home to most of the Legendary companions, and the one that deals in draw, damage and control all at once. The fastest way in is Full Release: sever a soul, open its pack. But the Veil remembers every door you open — release too many souls in a row and the debt comes due mid-run, when the next thing through the tear arrives twice as strong.

⚒ FORGE EVERY CARD TO ITS FINAL FORM

Cards aren't static — they're a ladder.

Every card climbs a six-star rank track of real, hand-authored upgrades that rewrite its numbers, its cost, and eventually its whole effect — and you can read the whole climb before you commit: right-click any card, anywhere it's offered, and it flips over in place — every rank it can reach printed on its back like a real card.

Push a Legendary companion to the top and it goes ASCENDED — a silver-electric form with an evolved signature ability:

  • Skyrend's pillars fall from the sky — unmissable, unblockable.

  • Grimm's every strike carries the rot his prey is already dying of.

  • The Wound Remembers sends a dying body's bleeding crawling into whatever rises next — landing as a blow of its own.

  • Find the rest.

👑 TWENTY-TWO NIGHTS. EIGHT BOSSES. ONE SECRET.

Each week ends at a boss that rewrites the rules.

  • THE CORONER mirrors your strikes — and, enraged, starts stealing the cards out of your deck.

  • THE QUARRY KING mortars himself in fresh stone every turn, until his blows crush straight through Block.

  • THE VEIL TYRANT cannot die at all — until he unfolds, wings blotting the candlelight, and his breath turns to fire.

Then the fourth week opens — and it is not the dead who came. The month ends under the Blood Moon or before the Wild Hunt, each with its own creatures, its own gate and its own master, and past them the one thing that was never meant to have a name.

Over a hundred kinds of dead stand between you and the dawn, and the nights themselves turn against you: omens that reshape the rules after dark, elite waves, and things that were never meant to have names. Survive the whole month, and the Veil finally shows you what it has been hiding.

Marks buy medallions on a permanent talent tree: three paths of claimed-forever power, from thicker skin to the Midnight Forge, each path crowned by a capstone that changes how every future run begins. Claim the Founder's Reliquary and a Legendary of your choosing rides in your starting deck. Forever.

📖 SIGN YOUR OWN CURSES

Deep enough down the tree, a hidden book opens.

THE LEDGER — its gold page sells permanent boons for everything you've ever banked. Its ash page is stranger: debts you sign against yourself.

  • Fight blind, with no enemy intents.

  • Let nothing heal you, all run.

  • Let your draw pile never refill — everything you play tonight is ash.

Every signed debt multiplies your score and your payout — stack the whole page and the game becomes a ×35 nightmare of your own design. The Ash Page of the leaderboard remembers who signed what.

Conquer the world, one fry at a time

Greaselord is a satirical strategy game: you build the biggest fast food empire in the world and spread across land, sea and air. But the bigger you get, the faster the health authorities move in with a worldwide fast food ban, and three rival chains want to take your countries away from you. Conquer 80% of the world market before one of them stops you.

Found your chain

Give your chain a name and a logo, pick one of 14 main dishes – from burgers, pizza and hot dogs to fried chicken, tacos, wok noodles and donuts – and your headquarters in one of 169 countries and territories. Each dish appeals to different customers and is popular in different regions. Neighbors, local tastes and the world situation of the round determine how fast you grow.

Pick your focus

Budget draws the masses, but cheap fat and sugar set the health authorities on your neck. Premium earns more from fewer customers, but makes enemies of the big chains. Fast Expansion grows everywhere at once through franchise partners, but they keep most of the money abroad. Every focus has its own opponent.

Features

  • Spread by land, sea and air: Once your market share in a country is high enough, its neighbors open up. Logistics upgrades unlock new markets sooner.

  • Eight population groups: teens, seniors, commuters, families, night owls, students, foodies and bargain hunters. A country only grows as far as your menu serves its people.

  • Menu tree with choices: Unlock sauces, sides and addictive extras. Some entries are mutually exclusive. Addiction boosts growth and revenue, but speeds up the health ban.

  • Secret Sauce and Black Budget: Click the burger bubbles above your countries before they disappear and use them to pay for your menu and for Government, Security and Sabotage upgrades. Surplus money flows into the Black Budget: Expansion Blitz, advertising, buyouts of local food joints, bribery.

  • Fend off three rivals: Shoot down their cargo planes, sink their ships, collect the loot and click their logo in time when they try to take over one of your countries. Lost a country? Win it back.

  • Outwit the health ban: Inspectors announce their visits, local bans hit individual foods, and from 60% market share the world fights back. Lobbyists, bribes and health weeks slow the ban down. At 100% the round is lost.

  • A different world every round: A burger fever in Asia, a sugar tax in Europe: every round starts with its own world situation, and trends change tastes, growth and costs. A news ticker with hundreds of headlines comments on your rise.

  • Rewards: Every round played to the end pays into your Rewards account. Spend it on purely cosmetic skins: ships, planes, loot, routes and shot effects.

Victory or defeat

Reach 80% of the world market to win. You lose if the health ban reaches 100%, the rival chains conquer the world before you do, you stay in debt for a whole year, or rivals push you out of your headquarters. You can pause or speed up the game at any time.

Game details

Single-player strategy game for Windows, playable with mouse and keyboard or an Xbox controller (also on Steam Deck), user interface in 103 languages.

Notes

Greaselord is a satire: the chains, their logos and the headlines are fictional. The world map, country borders and country data reflect the state of 2019, when development began. They are not updated and are not a political statement.
